says: The machine_path pattern's first branch, a slash, Users or home, then a slash, is not anchored to the start of a path, so a made-up fixture path whose second folder is named home (under a root folder named test) counts as a leak.
proof: A file holding one line that names brain.plist under the made-up root test, then home, checked with leakgrep.sh --text, prints 'leakgrep: leak machine_path at added line 1' and exits 1. The commit check on pull request 1079 exited 1 with three such hits in commit 259d4c655, all fixture paths under that made-up root, and an earlier push of 1079 needed its fixture folder renamed to brain-home to pass. This row itself first failed the check for quoting the path.
cost: A lead must hand-read every hit under a made-up root, or rename honest fixtures to dodge the check, and a hand-waved hit is how a real leak gets through.
